answer: A proof-of-space protocol deters Sybil attacks by requiring agents to commit unique cryptographic tables to persistent storage. As audit probes wander across assigned sectors, nodes must return integrity proofs rooted in a genesis relic within strict timeouts. An adversary creating fake identities faces a steep expenditure spiral, as allocating scarce physical disk space cannot be deduplicated or faked. However, this design accelerates drive degradation and excludes lightweight edge devices.
